chapter: Brass band style, leadership and recording
title: Bop, his idols and keeping his own voice
summary: He tried bop, names idols including Alvin Alcorn, Clifford Brown and Cat Anderson, and says his horn voice is his own.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Yeah. How does, we're talking about different types of music. Did you buy into the bop craze? Did you play into the bop music in the late 40s?

My mind is there. My mind is there. Because I was a youngster there, you know? So I play right now. I don't know what people see about my playing. I don't care because I play myself. I don't like to imitate nobody. My thoughts are my thoughts. Some of my idols was Alvin Alcorn, locally. Again, Wallace, Tompott, Emory Thompson, Clifford Brown. I love the way Clifford played. I love some other Howard McGee, Cat Anderson. All these guys I like. I like to hear them. I like to, some of the things they do, I like to say that I'm imitating, but in my own voice.
How do you differentiate? What are you doing different, you know?
Well, coming from me, it's got to be different. Coming from them, it's them.
Is there a different way that you attack the horn?

I would probably interpret it, yeah. I probably would interpret it differently. I'd have to because we all don't speak. My voice is not the same. So the horn voice is my voice. And it's not going to be the same. It may be similar. I may try something similar or get as close. But it's not going to be the same.
